name: singleton example uses the reference-corrected preference gap
test:
import math
import torch

def t(values, grad=False):
    return torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=grad)

def close(actual, expected):
    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=2e-5, atol=2e-6)

pc, pr, rc, rr = t([-2.], True), t([-4.], True), t([-3.]), t([-4.])
loss = dpo_loss(pc, pr, rc, rr, beta=0.5)
assert loss.shape == () and loss.dtype == torch.float32
assert loss.device.type == 'cpu'
close(loss, t(math.log1p(math.exp(-0.5))))
gc, gr = torch.autograd.grad(loss, (pc, pr))
close(gc, t([-0.5 / (1 + math.exp(0.5))]))
close(gr, -gc)
print("ok")

name: reference preferences matter and are frozen
input: reference inputs require gradients; policy favors chosen but reference favors it more
test:
import math
import torch

def t(values, grad=False):
    return torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=grad)

def close(actual, expected):
    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=2e-5, atol=2e-6)

pc, pr = t([-1., -3.], True), t([-3., -3.], True)
rc, rr = t([-1., -5.], True), t([-5., -1.], True)
before = [x.detach().clone() for x in (pc, pr, rc, rr)]
loss = dpo_loss(pc, pr, rc, rr, beta=0.5)
# Policy gaps [2,0], reference gaps [4,-4], z=[-1,2].
close(loss, t((1 + math.log1p(math.exp(-1)) + math.log1p(math.exp(-2))) / 2))
grads = torch.autograd.grad(loss, (pc, pr, rc, rr), allow_unused=True)
close(grads[0], t([-0.5 / (2 * (1 + math.exp(z))) for z in [-1, 2]]))
close(grads[1], -grads[0])
assert all(g is None or torch.count_nonzero(g) == 0 for g in grads[2:])
assert all(torch.equal(x.detach(), old) for x, old in zip((pc, pr, rc, rr), before))
print("ok")

name: beta scales the corrected gap before the logistic loss
test:
import math
import torch

def t(values, grad=False):
    return torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=grad)

def close(actual, expected):
    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=2e-5, atol=2e-6)

for beta in (0.01, 0.5, 2., 10.):
    pc, pr = t([-1.], True), t([-4.], True)
    loss = dpo_loss(pc, pr, t([-2.]), t([-3.]), beta=beta)
    close(loss, t(math.log1p(math.exp(-2 * beta))))
    gc, gr = torch.autograd.grad(loss, (pc, pr))
    close(gc, t([-beta / (1 + math.exp(2 * beta))]))
    close(gr, -gc)
print("ok")

name: extreme log-probabilities keep loss and gradients finite
test:
import math
import torch

def t(values, grad=False):
    return torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=grad)

def close(actual, expected):
    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=2e-5, atol=2e-6)

pc, pr = t([-10000., 0., -10000.], True), t([0., -10000., -10000.], True)
loss = dpo_loss(pc, pr, t([0., -10000., -10000.]), t([-10000., 0., -10000.]), beta=10.)
assert torch.isfinite(loss)
close(loss, t((200000 + math.log(2)) / 3))
gc, gr = torch.autograd.grad(loss, (pc, pr))
assert torch.isfinite(gc).all() and torch.isfinite(gr).all()
close(gc, t([-10 / 3, 0., -5 / 3]))
close(gr, -gc)
print("ok")

name: common offsets cancel and the full batch range is supported
input: B=256; sum reduction, exponentiating sequence log-probs, and input mutation are incorrect
test:
import math
import torch

def t(values, grad=False):
    return torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=grad)

def close(actual, expected):
    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=2e-5, atol=2e-6)

pc = torch.linspace(-5, -2, 256).requires_grad_()
pr = torch.linspace(-4, -3, 256).requires_grad_()
rc, rr = torch.full((256,), -4.), torch.full((256,), -5.)
before = [x.detach().clone() for x in (pc, pr, rc, rr)]
loss = dpo_loss(pc, pr, rc, rr, beta=0.3)
logits = [0.3 * ((float(c) - float(r)) - 1) for c, r in zip(pc.detach(), pr.detach())]
expected = sum(math.log1p(math.exp(-z)) for z in logits) / 256
close(loss, t(expected))
shifted = dpo_loss(pc - 100, pr - 100, rc - 20, rr - 20, beta=0.3)
close(shifted, loss)
assert all(torch.equal(x.detach(), old) for x, old in zip((pc, pr, rc, rr), before))
print("ok")
